strings.name: Joshua Angrist
strings.summary: Angrist identifies causal effects through policy changes, lotteries and institutional rules, especially in education and labor markets. With Guido Imbens he developed the local average treatment effect framework; collaborations with Krueger, Pischke and others advanced applied econometrics and teaching. A longtime MIT scholar, he received one-quarter of the 2021 economics Nobel. Hebrew University awarded him an honorary doctorate in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed causal-inference and natural-experiment methods, influencing education, labor and public-policy evaluation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Economics BA, Oberlin (1982); economics PhD, Princeton (1989).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Identifying natural experiments
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Imbens, clarified when instruments identify average causal effects for particular participants.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Evaluating education and labor policy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses institutional rules, lotteries and administrative data to study schooling, employment and policy.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Honorary doctorate conferred
strings.timeline.t1.text: Hebrew University awarded the honorary degree at its October 19 governors’ meeting.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Shared economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t2.text: He and Imbens shared half the prize for causal methods; David Card received the other half.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Coauthored Mastering ’Metrics
strings.timeline.t3.text: With Pischke, explained causal inference and applied econometrics through accessible examples.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published Mostly Harmless Econometrics
strings.timeline.t4.text: Coauthored with Pischke a methods book for empirical researchers.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joined MIT permanently
strings.timeline.t5.text: After an earlier visiting period, took a continuing faculty appointment in 1996.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Local average treatment effects
strings.timeline.t6.text: Published with Imbens an account of instrumental-variable estimates under imperfect compliance.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earned Princeton doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed economics doctoral training before beginning a Harvard faculty position.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed Oberlin studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned highest honors in economics before later labor-economics research.
